items.prompt:
Temperature measures the average kinetic energy of a sample's:
A) Color
B) Particles
C) Weight
D) Shape

steps: Temperature reflects the average kinetic energy of particles.

items.prompt:
The same heat is added to a small cup and a large pot of water. Which gets hotter?
A) The large pot
B) The small cup
C) Both equal
D) Neither

steps: Less mass heats up more for the same energy.

items.prompt:
A larger mass of water needs ___ energy to reach the same temperature change.
A) Less
B) More
C) No
D) Negative

Which two factors affect how much a sample's temperature rises for a given energy?
A) Color and shape
B) Mass and type of material
C) Name and age
D) Height and width
items.answer: B) Mass and type of material

steps: Mass and the material determine the temperature rise.

items.prompt:
Higher temperature means the particles have a higher:
A) Average kinetic energy
B) Color
C) Mass
D) Charge

steps: Temperature measures average particle kinetic energy.

items.prompt:
Why does a small cup of water heat faster than a large pot on the same burner?
A) It has more mass
B) It has less mass, so the same energy raises its temperature more
C) Water does not heat
D) The pot is colder
items.answer: B) It has less mass, so the same energy raises its temperature more

steps: Less mass means a larger temperature rise for the same energy.

items.prompt:
Why does the ocean change temperature more slowly than a small puddle?
A) The ocean has less mass
B) The ocean has much more mass, needing much more energy to change temperature
C) Puddles never change
D) Mass does not matter
items.answer: B) The ocean has much more mass, needing much more energy to change temperature

steps: Large mass requires much more energy to change temperature.

items.prompt:
How are temperature and thermal energy different?
A) They are the same
B) Temperature is the average particle energy; thermal energy is the total
C) Thermal energy is an average
D) Temperature is a total
items.answer: B) Temperature is the average particle energy; thermal energy is the total

steps: Temperature is an average; thermal energy is the total of all particles.
